name: logstalgia
desc: Web server access log visualizer with retro style
why: Turning web server access logs into a Pong-like animated stream of requests is a strange and satisfying way to watch traffic.

brief.what_it_is: Logstalgia is a website traffic visualizer that replays or streams web-server access logs as a Pong-like animation. Each request is drawn as a colored ball, colored to match the requesting host, that travels across the screen to the requested location. It reads standard Apache and Nginx access log formats (NCSA Common, Combined, and virtual-host variants), a pipe-delimited custom format, or live input on STDIN. The output is an on-screen animation rather than a file or report.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a way to watch a busy website's traffic as a never-ending torrent of requests, a pong-like battle between the web server and its visitors. It is pitched as a dashboard for work use, and the author invites contact about bespoke visualization work.
brief.how_it_works: Successful requests are hit by the paddle, while unsuccessful ones such as 404 File Not Found are missed and pass through. Paths are summarized by finding common path prefixes, and related paths are grouped under headings; by default, paths ending in png, gif or jpg fall under 'Images', and everything else goes to 'Miscellaneous'. Logs can be replayed from a file or followed live, for example by piping tail -f into it.

commands_seen.context: Watches the bundled example access log with default settings.
Follows a live Apache log, starting from the most recent batch of entries. The trailing '-' tells logstalgia to read from STDIN.
Follows the log in real time, starting from the next entry received on STDIN.
Watches a remote log over ssh, grouping URLs containing '/adclick.php' under the heading 'Ad Clicks'.

brief.install_notes: Requires a video card with OpenGL, so it is best run on a workstation rather than on the web server itself. The homepage offers a Windows setup.exe and zip for 1.0.9, and a source tarball logstalgia-1.1.5.tar.gz for 1.1.5. Building from source needs SDL 2 (1.2 support was removed), GLM and Boost headers (Boost 1.69 or newer as of 1.1.5), libpng, GLEW, and PCRE2. The homepage does not give full build steps and points to an INSTALL file that I did not read. No accounts or runtime configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: Turning a Pong-style game into a log viewer is an unusual choice, and the paddle mechanic carries meaning: a 404 visibly gets through the defense. Prefix-based path summarization also keeps a busy site's many URLs readable on one screen.
brief.status: maintained. The latest release, 1.1.5, is dated 4 March 2026, and the news section also shows 1.1.4 in January 2023 and 1.1.3 in June 2022. Releases are irregular, with a long gap between 2018 and 2022, but the project is clearly still active.
brief.caveats: Needs OpenGL, so it is not meant for headless servers. The README says it is designed for real-time playback and needs a fairly busy log (hundreds of requests per minute) to look interesting. Tailing remote logs is 'not currently recommended on the Windows version due to buffering issues'. Wayland support is listed as experimental. The README says nothing about license terms. Some of the README's more specific options, such as the --sync and -g flags, appear without a full reference on the homepage.
